text:
anya: heads-up: saw a puzzling warmup mismatch on canary where the runtime loaded a model with identical blob names but different internal chunk maps, causing tensor dupes and OOM during prefetched KV population.
jon: wait identical blob names? how did that happen? we dedupe uploads by content-hash at ingest.
anya: that's the issue. the uploader's client-side dedupe collapsed two distinct shard compositions produced by different packers that hashed to same content because packers reorder compressed chunks deterministically. runtime assumed chunk map from catalog matched blob layout but it didn't.
sasha: so the catalog pointed to a chunk-map that referenced logical offsets not matching the deduped physical artifact. loader resolved offsets wrong and ended up mapping two tensors to overlapping ranges.
kevin: yikes. root cause: dedupe was blind to chunk-map metadata. packer A and packer B produced semantically different maps but identical binary payload after compression and reorder. catalog referenced map from packerA but object store returned blob from packerB due to dedupe.
diego: possible fixes: 1) make dedupe include chunk-map fingerprint (sidecar) into content-hash; 2) runtime should verify sidecar map checksum against blob content before trusting mmap offsets; 3) make packers canonical so identical semantics -> identical binary.
rachel: tradeoffs: (1) breaks cross-account dedupe benefits and increases storage; (2) (2) adds verification cost on coldstart, but safe; (3) requires coord across toolchain.
jon: we should prioritize safety: runtime must not mmap offsets until it verifies the chunk-map matches actual blob layout. verification can be cheap: sample a few key offsets and check magic bytes or checksums per chunk. if mismatch, fallback to streaming.
sasha: agree. propose a two-level check: fast probabilistic validate_map(blob, map) -> true/false with low cost (read N small ranges), then a full verify for critical cases. fast check uses 1-2 range reads per chunk but capped to M ranges overall to avoid explosion.
kevin: how to handle dedupe semantics? vendors like S3 will dedupe only within account if we include metadata, but cross-account dedupe is beneficial. maybe dedupe should be keyed on (blob_binary_hash, chunkmap_hash) tuple; that preserves savings when chunkmap identical and prevents semantic mismatch. uploader can attach chunkmap_hash as metadata so object-store dedupe layer can consider it.
diego: also need a runtime metric and alert: chunkmap_mismatch_count and chunkmap_mismatch_rate. if mismatch spikes, we can throttle eager mmap and force full verify for future loads.
rachel: migration plan: a) immediate runtime patch: probabilistic validate_map + graceful fallback to streaming and metric + alert. b) uploader change: include chunkmap_hash in manifest and optional object metadata. c) catalog writer: include canonical chunkmap fingerprint and prefer canonical packer.
jon: QA: add an integration test where two different packers create different chunk maps but identical compressed payload; ensure runtime detects mismatch and falls back quietly. add a chaos test that enables object-store dedupe on ingest.
sasha: developer ergonomics: when mismatch happens, attach a short diagnostic in logs with model_id, artifact_etag, catalog_chunkmap_hash, observed_chunkmap_hash_probe, and the sample offsets that failed. keep it privacy-safe.
kevin: security: if we rely on sidecar chunkmap metadata for mmap offsets, ensure we verify signatures before applying offsets. otherwise a malicious actor could trick runtimes into mapping wrong ranges.
diego: operational note: set default fast-verify cap to 64KB of range reads per artifact on coldstart to limit cost. tune by observed mismatch-rate.
rachel: rollout: feature-flag REDWOOD_CHUNKMAP_SAFE_MMAP=on for canaries. after 2 weeks of stable metrics migrate default to on.
anya: I'll draft short RFC that captures: chunkmap-aware dedupe guidance, probabilistic_map_verify algorithm, metadata keys for uploader/catalog, metrics/alerts, and migration steps. who wants to co-author?
jon: i'll take the uploader/catalog sections.
sasha: i'll do the runtime verify alg and tests. kevin: i'll own metrics and runbook. diego: i'll help with benchmarks for the probe cost.
dev-bot: RFC draft created: /r/chunkmap-aware-dedupe-and-safe-mmap (link pinned to #eng-ml). :white_check_mark:
anya: thanks all 44d I'll post the RFC link and a checklist once the draft lands.
